        author = "SOC Team"

        uint16(0) == 0x5a4d and any of ($s*) and $x64_cfg
}

arguments.summary: A sophisticated phishing campaign led to a Cobalt Strike beacon implant on a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042). The attacker leveraged malicious PowerShell execution from Outlook to deploy an unsigned DLL, establishing command and control (C2) communication over HTTPS to a known-bad IP. Lateral movement was attempted via SMB to a file server. Concurrently, anomalous activity from the 'admin_backup' account, including unusual login times, geolocation, and privilege escalation attempts on the domain controller, indicates potential credential compromise and privilege escalation. The initial access vector was traced to an emergency access request from a compromised source IP.

rundll32.exe loads and executes the beacon.dll, establishing C2 channel.
Hosts file is modified to block security-related domains (T1565.001).
IDS alerts on Cobalt Strike C2 traffic (ET TROJAN signature).
Lateral movement attempt via SMB to file server WS-FIN-050 (partially successful).
UEBA system flags 'admin_backup' account for anomalous behavior (unusual time, Bucharest VPN).
Emergency access request triggers initial high-severity alert, initiating this investigation.
